title: M/S Shree Ganpati Electricals v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Alok Mathur, J. and Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal, J.
disposition: Interim temporary connection under clause 4.10; writ listed
headnote: On a writ against refusal of a fresh shop connection for premises dues under clauses 4.3 and 4.4 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the Court, prima facie treating one of three independent shops as a separate premise, directed respondent no. 2 to give a temporary connection under clause 4.10 within 24 hours of an application made in two working days, and listed the petition.
facts: M/S Shree Ganpati Electricals took a vacant shop at S1-1396, Suraksha Enclave, Saheed Path, Lucknow and applied to Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. for a fresh connection. On 3 June 2024 the application was rejected for premises dues under clauses 4.3 and 4.4 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petitioner said the address held three independent shops, two with separate running connections. The licensee produced a bill of Rs.2,68,659 dated 27 February 2021 on account no. 8690847573; the notice recorded that the other shop's bill had been paid.

holding_units.holding: As an interim measure, if the petitioner applies within two working days, respondent no. 2 shall provide a temporary electricity connection within 24 hours under clause 4.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, in accordance with law.
holding_units.flag: Cited as clause 4.10 without a sub-clause; not matched to 4.10(a) or 4.10(e).

principle_tags.application: While the challenge to refusal of a fresh connection under clauses 4.3 and 4.4 remained pending, the Court directed a temporary connection under clause 4.10 within 24 hours of an application filed within two working days.

not_decided.point: Whether clauses 4.3 and 4.4 bar a fresh connection to one independent shop because dues remain against other shops at the same address
not_decided.note: Only a prima facie view was recorded that the shop was a separate premise. Counter-affidavit and rejoinder were called, and the writ was listed on 8 August 2024.
